recentItems.title: Blackmore fires damage properties, residents forced to flee in Darwin's rural area | ABC NEWS
recentItems.description:
Bushfires Northern Territory has downgraded an emergency warning for a fire at Stockwell Road in Blackmore, south of Darwin, to a watch and act.

Acting Chief Fire Control Officer Nathaniel Stanford said this afternoon some structures had reportedly been "engulfed" but details were yet to be confirmed.

Residents are advised that there is still a "heightened level of threat" and they should "remain vigilant into the evening". Roxanne Fitzgerald has this update for ABC Northern Territory.

recentItems.title: Anthropic signs agreement for $32b data centre in Queensland | ABC NEWS
recentItems.description:
AI giant Anthropic has signed an agreement to use part of a $32 billion data centre proposed for a site on Queensland's Western Downs.
The project is set to be the largest of its kind in Australia and will draw as much power as about 1.5 million average Australian households.
Premier David Crisafulli has promised the centre will put more energy into the grid and drive down power prices for Queenslanders.

recentItems.title: AI fears unite political enemies in Washington as Donald Trump resists pressure to act | ABC NEWS
recentItems.description:
Right-wing podcaster Steve Bannon and left-wing US senator Bernie Sanders have spoken at a Washington event on the dangers of AI and the need for regulation.

US President Donald Trump phoned into a separate event to reinforce his opposition to intervening and repeat his claim that AI warnings represented a "hoax".

Senator Sanders will introduce a bill that would pause advanced AI development, but similar attempts to legislate have stalled in Congress in recent years.

recentItems.title: The heavy-handed tactics used to force people to pay debts | The Business | ABC NEWS
recentItems.description:
An ABC investigation has uncovered the case of an 81-yea2r-old woman, who was bullied and intimidated by Suncorp's debt collector ARMA Group over a debt she didn't owe.

Diane Walker started receiving debt collection notices after a minor car accident in which she was not at fault. The other driver's insurer AAMI, part of the Suncorp Group, contacted her to cover costs.

But when Ms Walker pushed back, asking for evidence,which Suncorp didn't have, It engaged ARMA Group. 

Next came a number of legal threats.

ARMA Group is one of Australia's largest debt collectors, supporting more than 1,000 businesses to recover money.

It uses automatic processes and its website recently said it takes "less than two minutes to set up a smart payment plan and no manual intervention is required."

Diane Walker's son, Scott stepped in to help. He's previously worked as freelance camera operator for the ABC.

ARMA Group didn't respond to repeated questions from the ABC. Further contact was made with its executives, who also didn't comment.

The consumer watchdog is taking action against ARMA Group in the Federal Court.  The ACCC is alleging it and Force Legal, which are both owned by Credit Clear Limited, sent 320,000 debt enforcement notices to individuals that were misleading.

Former ACCC chair Allan Fels says it's "Robodebt 2.0 of the worst form....this seems to be the worst kind of illegal, deceptive conduct, applied to bully, intimidate and frighten."

Diane Walker case is now resolved. Suncorp apologised and compensated her with a $1,500 goodwill fee.

It also told her that ARMA had acknowledged the matter was not handled appropriately.
#ABCBusiness
